topic: Strange borders countdown: Perejil goat island and 6 more
hook: Two European countries nearly went to war over a rock with goats on it, and soldiers were sent in by helicopter.
title: 7 Insane Borders, Including a War Over Goats
description:
Spain and Morocco nearly went to war in 2002 over Perejil, a bare goat island. This countdown also visits a runway that cars cross, a Spanish town inside France, a German village inside Switzerland, and ends on the tangled India-Bangladesh enclaves. Every border here is real, and you can find each one on a map.

#borders #geography #mapfacts

scenes.narration: Two European countries nearly went to war over a rock with goats on it, and soldiers were sent in by helicopter.
scenes.headline: War Over Goats

scenes.narration: That is not a joke, and it is not a movie plot. It really happened in the year 2002.
scenes.headline: It Really Happened

scenes.narration: In this video you will see seven borders that make no sense, from runways to enclaves.
scenes.headline: 7 Borders

scenes.narration: One of them cuts a runway in half, and one hides a whole town inside another country.
scenes.headline: Runway And Hidden Town

scenes.narration: But the strangest of all is in India, and it involves land that changed countries at midnight.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest

scenes.narration: We will count down from seven to one, and every border is stranger than the last.
scenes.headline: Countdown 7 To 1

scenes.narration: So stay until the end, because the goat island is only number three.
scenes.headline: Goat Island Is #3

scenes.narration: Let us start at number seven, with a runway that a road crosses.
scenes.headline: Let's Start

scenes.narration: Number seven: a road that stops for airplanes. This is Gibraltar, a small British territory on the southern tip of Spain.
scenes.headline: Gibraltar

scenes.narration: Right at the Spanish border, the main road runs straight across the airport runway.
scenes.headline: Road Across Runway

scenes.narration: When a plane is about to land, barriers come down and cars, bikes and walkers all wait.
scenes.headline: Barriers Come Down

scenes.narration: Then the plane lands, the barriers go up, and everyone carries on, as if nothing happened.
scenes.headline: Then Everyone Walks On

scenes.narration: The runway was built on a narrow strip of land during the Second World War.
scenes.headline: Built In WWII

scenes.narration: Spain does not accept that Britain owns that strip, so the airport itself sits on disputed land.
scenes.headline: Disputed Land

scenes.narration: So you can stand at a border crossing and watch a jet roll by a few metres away.
scenes.headline: Jet Beside The Border

scenes.narration: Passports are checked on foot, and then you walk straight over the runway to enter town.
scenes.headline: Walk Over The Runway

scenes.narration: That is odd, but at number six, a whole Spanish town is hiding inside France.
scenes.headline: Next: Inside France

scenes.narration: Number six: a Spanish town that sits entirely inside France. It is called Llívia, in the Pyrenees mountains.
scenes.headline: Llívia

scenes.narration: Look at the map and you will see a small Spanish island, with France on every side.
scenes.headline: Spanish Island In France

scenes.narration: The reason goes back to a treaty in 1659, when Spain gave France a group of villages.
scenes.headline: Treaty Of 1659

scenes.narration: But Llívia was officially a town, not a village, so the treaty never took it away.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: That tiny wording difference is why it is still Spanish more than three hundred years later.
scenes.headline: One Word Decided It

scenes.narration: A neutral road links Llívia to Spain, so Spanish drivers can travel there without entering France.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: Llívia even has one of the oldest pharmacies in Europe, in a Spanish town surrounded by France.
scenes.headline: Old Pharmacy

scenes.narration: A border shaped by one missing word, and it is still on the map today.
scenes.headline: Still On The Map

scenes.narration: Next, a village where people pay with two different currencies, because Switzerland is all around them.
scenes.headline: Next: Two Currencies

scenes.narration: Number five: Büsingen, a German village with no land link to Germany at all.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: It is surrounded by Switzerland, so to reach the rest of Germany you must cross Swiss land.
scenes.headline: Ringed By Switzerland

scenes.narration: Büsingen is part of Germany, but it sits inside the Swiss customs area, so its shops follow Swiss rules.
scenes.headline: Swiss Customs Area

scenes.narration: Many shops accept Swiss francs as well as euros, so your wallet needs to be ready for both.
scenes.headline: Francs And Euros

scenes.narration: It even has its own car number plates, which start with the letters BÜS.
scenes.headline: Its Own Plates

scenes.narration: In 1918 most villagers voted to join Switzerland, but Switzerland refused.
scenes.headline: Voted For Switzerland

scenes.narration: So they stayed German, in the middle of Switzerland, where they still live today.
scenes.headline: Still German

scenes.narration: It is a quiet village, but it proves a border can wrap around a place like a ring.
scenes.headline: Border Like A Ring

scenes.narration: Now for a place in North America that you can only drive to by leaving your own country.
scenes.headline: Next: Leave To Get Home

scenes.narration: Number four: Point Roberts, an American town you can only reach by road through Canada.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: It sits on the tip of a small peninsula, just south of a straight line drawn on the map.
scenes.headline: A Straight Line

scenes.narration: That line is the forty-ninth parallel, chosen as the border long ago by treaty.
scenes.headline: 49th Parallel

scenes.narration: The line was straight, so it cut the peninsula, and the tip ended up in the United States.
scenes.headline: Peninsula Cut Off

scenes.narration: Today, to drive from Point Roberts to the rest of America, you must cross into Canada first.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Canada

scenes.narration: Then you cross back into the United States, which means two border checks for a normal trip.
scenes.headline: Two Border Checks

scenes.narration: If you enjoy strange maps like this, subscribe, because there are more places like these on the channel.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: A simple straight line created a town that is American on paper and Canadian by road.
scenes.headline: American On Paper

scenes.narration: And at number three, one rock nearly started a war between two friendly countries.
scenes.headline: Next: The Goat Island

scenes.narration: Number three: Perejil Island, the goat island. Its name is the Spanish word for parsley.
scenes.headline: Perejil Island

scenes.narration: It is a bare rock, with almost nothing on it, only about two hundred metres off the coast of Morocco.
scenes.headline: A Bare Rock

scenes.narration: Spain says it is Spanish, Morocco says it is Moroccan, and for decades nobody lived there.
scenes.headline: Who Owns It?

scenes.narration: Some goats grazed on the rock, and that was about all there was.
scenes.headline: Just Goats

scenes.narration: Then in July 2002, a small group of Moroccan soldiers landed there and set up a post.
scenes.headline: Soldiers Land

scenes.narration: Spain called it a hostile act, because Spain has its own city of Ceuta only a few kilometres away.
scenes.headline: Ceuta Is Spanish

scenes.narration: Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish cities on the African coast, and they are the only land borders between the EU and Africa.
scenes.headline: Spain In Africa

scenes.narration: Spain sent warships, and for days two neighbours stared at each other over a narrow stretch of sea.
scenes.headline: Warships Arrive

scenes.narration: On the morning of 17 July, Spanish special forces came in by helicopter and landed on the rock.
scenes.headline: Helicopters Land

scenes.narration: They removed the handful of Moroccan soldiers, and no one was killed.
scenes.headline: Nobody Killed

scenes.narration: Then American diplomats stepped in, and both sides agreed to go back to how things were before.
scenes.headline: US Steps In

scenes.narration: So today, the rock is empty again, with no flag, no troops and no one living there.
scenes.headline: Empty Again

scenes.narration: Two countries almost fought a war over a rock with no people and no buildings.
scenes.headline: Over A Bare Rock

scenes.narration: At number two, a region of Russia that cannot be reached by land from Russia.
scenes.headline: Next: Cut-Off Russia

scenes.narration: Number two: Kaliningrad, a part of Russia that is cut off from the rest of Russia.
scenes.headline: Kaliningrad

scenes.narration: It sits on the Baltic Sea, with Poland on one side and Lithuania on the other.
scenes.headline: Baltic Sea Coast

scenes.narration: After the Soviet Union broke up in 1991, the countries around it became independent.
scenes.headline: Soviet Union Ends

scenes.narration: That left Kaliningrad as a separate piece, far from the Russian mainland.
scenes.headline: A Separate Piece

scenes.narration: Travel between Kaliningrad and the rest of Russia by land means crossing other countries.
scenes.headline: Cross Other Countries

scenes.narration: Trains have had to cross Lithuania to get through, with special rules for the passengers.
scenes.headline: Train Through Lithuania

scenes.narration: Imagine a piece of your own state sitting across foreign lands, with no road to it at home.
scenes.headline: No Road Home

scenes.narration: But even this is not the strangest. For that, we need to go to India.
scenes.headline: Now, India

scenes.narration: Number one: the border enclaves of Cooch Behar, on the India and Bangladesh border.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar Enclaves

scenes.narration: For decades, small pieces of India lay inside Bangladesh, and small pieces of Bangladesh lay inside India.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: These pockets were called enclaves, and they were scattered across the border like puzzle pieces.
scenes.headline: Scattered Pockets

scenes.narration: People living in them were cut off from their own country, with no easy road to it.
scenes.headline: Cut Off

scenes.narration: Some villagers had little access to schools, hospitals or electricity, because the country around them did not govern their land.
scenes.headline: No Services

scenes.narration: It gets stranger. In one place, there was Indian land inside Bangladeshi land inside Indian land inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Four Layers

scenes.narration: That plot was called Dahala Khagrabari, and it is often called the only one of its kind in the world.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: At midnight on 31 July 2015, India and Bangladesh finally swapped these pockets of land.
scenes.headline: The Midnight Swap

scenes.narration: In total, one hundred and sixty-two enclaves changed hands, and about fifty thousand people had to choose.
scenes.headline: 162 Enclaves

scenes.narration: For many, it meant a proper address, a vote and access to services from the country they lived in.
scenes.headline: A Real Address

scenes.narration: It was one of the most tangled borders ever drawn, and it was right here in our own backyard.
scenes.headline: Most Tangled Border

scenes.narration: And that is why India has the strangest border of all, even if it was finally tidied up.
scenes.headline: India Wins

scenes.narration: So that is seven borders: a runway, a Spanish town in France, a German village in Switzerland, and more.
scenes.headline: All 7 Borders

scenes.narration: And remember the goat island: two countries, helicopters, warships, and nobody hurt over a bare rock.
scenes.headline: The Goat Island

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: the country that has no border at its own front door. See you then.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow
scenes.sub: No border at the front door
